title: Huawei USG IPS botnet alerts
volume: None on a normal day. An infected host beacons on a schedule, so expect several an hour from it, all in its case.
mdr_note: These detections are yours to work. Sophos MDR doesn't work custom detections, and a case your own case rule opens from them is Managed By Self.
author: Aaronjacobs000
summary: One custom detection rule for Huawei USG and HiSecEngine firewalls, on the NIDS records the library's Huawei USG parsers write from IPS logs. It makes a detection when the firewall's IPS sees botnet command and control traffic or a botnet domain lookup. It matches sensor type Huawei USG only.
notes:
Setup:
- Add the library's Huawei USG and HiSecEngine parsers and send the firewall's info-center logs to the data collector first, then run the check-your-data search to see logs arrive.
- Turn on IPS with botnet detection in the security policies that cover outbound traffic.

How it works:
- IPS/4/BOTNET logs, and IPS/4/DOMAIN logs of the Botnet category, both carry the classification Botnet, and the rule takes that classification, blocked or not.

Testing:
- In a lab tenant on 2026-11-23, each query returned exactly the sample lines tests.json lists in Data Lake Search, and the rules run offline on the same 4 records agreed. The samples went in with their dates moved to the day before the test, so they fell inside the search's time range.
- As live rules there, each one fired on exactly its sample lines. Lines sent in the first 12 minutes after the rules were made made no detection on line 8; sent again about 30 minutes after, they did.
- No Sophos detector made a detection on the lines these rules take. Sophos's sign-in analytics flagged only sample sign-ins on Auth, as an unseen user, address or application.

Known gaps:
- Other IPS detections, such as an attack on a server, aren't taken.
- A beacon the IPS has no signature for makes none.
